title: Watery diarrhoea or vomiting — put the water back in
applies_to: Someone with watery diarrhoea or repeated vomiting, who is losing more water than they are taking in.

citations.source: WHO Recommendations on the Clinical Management of Acute Diarrhoea
citations.section: Oral rehydration therapy and home-made solution

citations.source: WHO and UNICEF Joint Statement on the Clinical Management of Acute Diarrhoea
citations.section: Plan A: treat diarrhoea at home

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020

steps.text: Look for the signs of losing too much water. A dry mouth. Little or no urine. Sunken eyes. No tears when a child cries. Being very sleepy.
Give oral rehydration salts. They are sold in packets, marked ORS. Mix one into clean water, exactly as the packet says.
Give it in small sips. A spoonful every few minutes. Small sips stay down when a whole cup will not.
If they bring it back up, wait 10 minutes. Then start the small sips again.
If you have no packets, use 1 litre of clean water. Stir in 6 level teaspoons of sugar. Stir in half a level teaspoon of salt. Measure it well. Too much salt makes this worse.
Count how much they drink. Count how often they pass urine. Those two numbers tell you if this is working.
Keep feeding a child their normal food as well. Keep feeding a baby at the breast, as often as it wants.
Take them to a clinic if there is blood in what comes out. Go too if the vomiting will not stop, or they cannot keep any liquid down.
Call for help now if they are too sleepy to drink. Call now if they have passed no urine all day, or are breathing fast.

do_not: Do not give fizzy drinks, sweet juice, or energy drinks. Sugary liquid pulls more water into the gut and makes it worse.
Do not mix the salts with more or less water than the packet says. Too strong is dangerous, especially for a child.
Do not give a young child anything to stop the diarrhoea.
Do not stop giving liquid because they keep being sick. Keep offering small sips.
Do not use water you would not drink yourself. Boil it and let it cool if you are unsure.
escalate_if: They are a baby under 6 months, or an older adult — get them seen early rather than waiting.
They stop answering you properly, or the hands and feet go cold and blotchy — call for help now.
There is blood in the vomit or in the stool — they need a clinic today.
The diarrhoea is like white rice water and pouring out — say those words on the phone. That spreads to other people.
You have no clean water at all — tell the clinic that when you call, because it changes what they send.
